Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 39, "heading": "CHAPTER 37. A LITTLE COLD WATER", "previous_rows": [], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 37, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u039-h", "tag": "h2", "role": "heading", "text": "CHAPTER 37. A LITTLE COLD WATER", "sha256": "5550703fb6ea84e898521aeb28035efcec3f0c2a6e1aec3af0728b54627b0f9a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/h2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": []}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0001", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My new life had lasted for more than a week, and I was stronger than ever in those tremendous practical resolutions that I felt the crisis required. I continued to walk extremely fast, and to have a general idea that I was getting on. I made it a rule to take as much out of myself as I possibly could, in my way of doing everything to which I applied my energies. I made a perfect victim of myself. I even entertained some idea of putting myself on a vegetable diet, vaguely conceiving that, in becoming a graminivorous animal, I should sacrifice to Dora.", "sha256": "4960bd9a568833cf141aa049529e0e89f2a4e944003428469f69ed46543ccb93", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[1]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0002", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As yet, little Dora was quite unconscious of my desperate firmness, otherwise than as my letters darkly shadowed it forth. But another Saturday came, and on that Saturday evening she was to be at Miss Mills’s; and when Mr. Mills had gone to his whist-club (telegraphed to me in the street, by a bird-cage in the drawing-room middle window), I was to go there to tea.", "sha256": "109079701e3f21a0a1a69b1eb235feec969ec23960578f5800735615135d2294", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[2]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0003", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "By this time, we were quite settled down in Buckingham Street, where Mr. Dick continued his copying in a state of absolute felicity. My aunt had obtained a signal victory over Mrs. Crupp, by paying her off, throwing the first pitcher she planted on the stairs out of window, and protecting in person, up and down the staircase, a supernumerary whom she engaged from the outer world. These vigorous measures struck such terror to the breast of Mrs. Crupp, that she subsided into her own kitchen, under the impression that my aunt was mad. My aunt being supremely indifferent to Mrs. Crupp’s opinion and everybody else’s, and rather favouring than discouraging the idea, Mrs. Crupp, of late the bold, became within a few days so faint-hearted, that rather than encounter my aunt upon the staircase, she would endeavour to hide her portly form behind doors—leaving visible, however, a wide margin of flannel petticoat—or would shrink into dark corners. This gave my aunt such unspeakable satisfaction, that I believe she took a delight in prowling up and down, with her bonnet insanely perched on the top of her head, at times when Mrs. Crupp was likely to be in the way.", "sha256": "e265cf448bc9104779d39eeecd7649aefa35ae0defbaaf9a8cdccefdeb5a372b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[3]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0004", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt, being uncommonly neat and ingenious, made so many little improvements in our domestic arrangements, that I seemed to be richer instead of poorer. Among the rest, she converted the pantry into a dressing-room for me; and purchased and embellished a bedstead for my occupation, which looked as like a bookcase in the daytime as a bedstead could. I was the object of her constant solicitude; and my poor mother herself could not have loved me better, or studied more how to make me happy.", "sha256": "56950fb773616507127d8db6f0cd6980c43fb769031a21e28bb4b7fd1fa44b49", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[4]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0005", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Peggotty had considered herself highly privileged in being allowed to participate in these labours; and, although she still retained something of her old sentiment of awe in reference to my aunt, had received so many marks of encouragement and confidence, that they were the best friends possible. But the time had now come (I am speaking of the Saturday when I was to take tea at Miss Mills’s) when it was necessary for her to return home, and enter on the discharge of the duties she had undertaken in behalf of Ham. ‘So good-bye, Barkis,’ said my aunt, ‘and take care of yourself! I am sure I never thought I could be sorry to lose you!’", "sha256": "ae5ca8c803b06289aa5ebfba354674a200cb1c8affb77fe9f576e9aa3aa4fb4f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[5]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0006", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I took Peggotty to the coach office and saw her off. She cried at parting, and confided her brother to my friendship as Ham had done. We had heard nothing of him since he went away, that sunny afternoon.", "sha256": "56547e2a262d9ae91dce75640b03261edfd2149a0135d384b24a8f9c1089dadc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[6]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0007", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And now, my own dear Davy,’ said Peggotty, ‘if, while you’re a prentice, you should want any money to spend; or if, when you’re out of your time, my dear, you should want any to set you up (and you must do one or other, or both, my darling); who has such a good right to ask leave to lend it you, as my sweet girl’s own old stupid me!’", "sha256": "b9342109f9f28c1f4e297e079e8acb2ae7cd5c6138421f210b110a002ed6e906", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[7]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0008", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was not so savagely independent as to say anything in reply, but that if ever I borrowed money of anyone, I would borrow it of her. Next to accepting a large sum on the spot, I believe this gave Peggotty more comfort than anything I could have done.", "sha256": "e1f6838ad5791f14fd680e377240f74dc6211a67eb87ab688ed1ba8384016659", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[8]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0009", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And, my dear!’ whispered Peggotty, ‘tell the pretty little angel that I should so have liked to see her, only for a minute! And tell her that before she marries my boy, I’ll come and make your house so beautiful for you, if you’ll let me!’", "sha256": "ed7f674111cc8361d18a89a04b70c36866e41efa884fedffaf4d7163fd133f8f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[9]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0010", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I declared that nobody else should touch it; and this gave Peggotty such delight that she went away in good spirits.", "sha256": "05c9083e7f09b28b4e523fe2a1af6304bc8ead23c2132ed1f33aa29e2797d711", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[10]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0011", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I fatigued myself as much as I possibly could in the Commons all day, by a variety of devices, and at the appointed time in the evening repaired to Mr. Mills’s street. Mr. Mills, who was a terrible fellow to fall asleep after dinner, had not yet gone out, and there was no bird-cage in the middle window.", "sha256": "75bb83caa6d73567167b8941a210e85acd63414afe04bf6cec5e79542e146ae6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[11]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0012", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He kept me waiting so long, that I fervently hoped the Club would fine him for being late. At last he came out; and then I saw my own Dora hang up the bird-cage, and peep into the balcony to look for me, and run in again when she saw I was there, while Jip remained behind, to bark injuriously at an immense butcher’s dog in the street, who could have taken him like a pill.", "sha256": "cd8509b24e61b0179400da64308a2f4be9d0a459fa4ad18c8f8072c87acd1497", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[12]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0013", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Dora came to the drawing-room door to meet me; and Jip came scrambling out, tumbling over his own growls, under the impression that I was a Bandit; and we all three went in, as happy and loving as could be. I soon carried desolation into the bosom of our joys—not that I meant to do it, but that I was so full of the subject—by asking Dora, without the smallest preparation, if she could love a beggar?", "sha256": "6d4bdea2da26c9a757001d70618a76d3a55ffe8f5f83404ea904a365229b69fa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[13]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0014", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My pretty, little, startled Dora! Her only association with the word was a yellow face and a nightcap, or a pair of crutches, or a wooden leg, or a dog with a decanter-stand in his mouth, or something of that kind; and she stared at me with the most delightful wonder.", "sha256": "9e08152fbda93f8827ac6b2627d31d98f973e0ab3d2ac07e8278a4bd6aa5fca8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[14]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0015", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘How can you ask me anything so foolish?’ pouted Dora. ‘Love a beggar!’", "sha256": "aa1505a9da0bdb4219363ba0084e8dfe96e16492e354169d8bfc4c4bcb2db0a2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[15]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0016", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Dora, my own dearest!’ said I. ‘I am a beggar!’", "sha256": "6d3c3f4b762dfd3eebab20f20b59218a704dce0d536eb7890d73e09a1b4c0531", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[16]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0017", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘How can you be such a silly thing,’ replied Dora, slapping my hand, ‘as to sit there, telling such stories? I’ll make Jip bite you!’", "sha256": "745c404985c6d513daa30c3707e4f8b58084cd469dd341cb0a00e3e218b2b543", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[17]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0018", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Her childish way was the most delicious way in the world to me, but it was necessary to be explicit, and I solemnly repeated:", "sha256": "c9c99f04439247457ea0599b1bfc5810bcf5b7238954b8034f67c27d80214b4b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[18]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0019", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Dora, my own life, I am your ruined David!’", "sha256": "86e2725b873b79422610200b800c86ec5fdb6d01061dffe2621047123b5ebf01", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[19]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0020", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I declare I’ll make Jip bite you!’ said Dora, shaking her curls, ‘if you are so ridiculous.’", "sha256": "e49e2580b8907001de0589b906a8200942c560785170140db7a7db1f1546349b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[20]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0021", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But I looked so serious, that Dora left off shaking her curls, and laid her trembling little hand upon my shoulder, and first looked scared and anxious, then began to cry. That was dreadful. I fell upon my knees before the sofa, caressing her, and imploring her not to rend my heart; but, for some time, poor little Dora did nothing but exclaim Oh dear! Oh dear! And oh, she was so frightened! And where was Julia Mills! And oh, take her to Julia Mills, and go away, please! until I was almost beside myself.", "sha256": "35f55f04e24bbd53d694ca26bd4b1f1395ec4ce08e5fcbe05da2a38d8cf0a2a6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[21]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0022", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At last, after an agony of supplication and protestation, I got Dora to look at me, with a horrified expression of face, which I gradually soothed until it was only loving, and her soft, pretty cheek was lying against mine. Then I told her, with my arms clasped round her, how I loved her, so dearly, and so dearly; how I felt it right to offer to release her from her engagement, because now I was poor; how I never could bear it, or recover it, if I lost her; how I had no fears of poverty, if she had none, my arm being nerved and my heart inspired by her; how I was already working with a courage such as none but lovers knew; how I had begun to be practical, and look into the future; how a crust well earned was sweeter far than a feast inherited; and much more to the same purpose, which I delivered in a burst of passionate eloquence quite surprising to myself, though I had been thinking about it, day and night, ever since my aunt had astonished me.", "sha256": "d6d3a3caaf722cd26c412c3e69912040bd01293462116dd4db493ba290c87007", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[22]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0023", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Is your heart mine still, dear Dora?’ said I, rapturously, for I knew by her clinging to me that it was.", "sha256": "c434110b2d677531154a4be5e299874608dc9ae4a2b1e5fe2615a9c831fe99cb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[23]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0024", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, yes!’ cried Dora. ‘Oh, yes, it’s all yours. Oh, don’t be dreadful!’", "sha256": "bcf12e534867a3e26f7bff72c372bcd57e018250acbdb9b4e7c648328c6a471a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[24]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0025", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I dreadful! To Dora!", "sha256": "5c2903a26e762c0bd930349feadacfcc3e3d60e99e524f050c8370f58290cf70", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[25]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0026", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Don’t talk about being poor, and working hard!’ said Dora, nestling closer to me. ‘Oh, don’t, don’t!’", "sha256": "fb52a30ace37c43171ddb991437186e92fd7a3c91b4c5e56bba893c973a7926a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[26]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0027", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dearest love,’ said I, ‘the crust well-earned—’", "sha256": "6e811d4ba3e2a52db4fda362f60b2bf81585bad6b14c4f7122de56ae64863100", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[27]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0028", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, yes; but I don’t want to hear any more about crusts!’ said Dora. ‘And Jip must have a mutton-chop every day at twelve, or he’ll die.’", "sha256": "3a3092c4ee7a6dcca4b5f88c85c7be2f563eb76b0fd9fa320fc641dde0c9f13a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[28]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0029", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was charmed with her childish, winning way. I fondly explained to Dora that Jip should have his mutton-chop with his accustomed regularity. I drew a picture of our frugal home, made independent by my labour—sketching in the little house I had seen at Highgate, and my aunt in her room upstairs.", "sha256": "dfc91c04f64953e1d8ed839f7ab18abfba9df4e259e0b0548a15ef9d03c76b3c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[29]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0030", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am not dreadful now, Dora?’ said I, tenderly.", "sha256": "6a82bba196df0f8eab871b749dfa21c61584e6dcf2b37cd5903e17b91bc87e92", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[30]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0031", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, no, no!’ cried Dora. ‘But I hope your aunt will keep in her own room a good deal. And I hope she’s not a scolding old thing!’", "sha256": "07da5d92303df150fc6c1e8bb5f3ebaf87437a99b9866bd20958f8de65f41bc8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[31]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
